meta.purpose: What real German datacenters do now. New studies and technologies are added as scenarios and compared against this baseline.

conventions.fact: Every number is an object: { value, unit, status, source, asOf, note? }. 'source' is a key in 'sources' (or a list of keys). Derived facts carry 'formula' and 'inputs' instead of a single source.

statuses.reported: Self-reported by the operator to the German datacenter register (RZReg). Official filing, not independently audited.
statuses.permitted: Fixed in an official permit or binding plan (a limit or an approved design). Says what is allowed or built, not what is measured.
statuses.operator: Stated by the operator in its own press release or website.
statuses.derived: Calculated by us from other values in this file. Formula and inputs are listed.
statuses.regulation: A legal requirement currently in force.
statuses.draft-law: In a government bill that has not passed parliament.
statuses.reference: Official statistic used for everyday comparisons.
statuses.vendor-claim: A manufacturer's claim, not yet confirmed by independent operation.
statuses.not-public: Exists, but is not published. The entry says where it is held and how it could be requested.
statuses.study: A published study. The source says who commissioned it (government, industry or independent).
statuses.chosen: A choice made for a model, not a measured or reported value (used for the fictional ideal datacenter).

conventions.wue: WUE = litres of water per kWh of IT energy (EN 50600-4-9 / EnEfG). IT energy is not in the register, so we approximate it as total energy / PUE.

verdicts.depends: True in some cases, not others.
verdicts.not-supported: The evidence does not back it as stated.
verdicts.no-data: There is not enough public evidence to say.

vantage-fra21.name: Vantage FRA21

location.region: Frankfurt Rhine-Main, next to Frankfurt Airport

opened.value: completed by 2022-11-03 (first building on the Frankfurt II campus)

floorArea.note: Register 'surface area'. Differs from the operator's 33,000 m²; the two likely measure different things. Neither definition is stated.

totalEnergy.note: Largest total energy use of all 322 sites in the register.

renewableShare.note: Renewable energy factor (REF): balance-sheet renewable electricity, not on-site generation.

coolingEfficiencyRatio.note: Heat removed per unit of cooling energy. Higher is better.

wasteHeatTemp.note: Too cool to heat homes directly; would need heat pumps.

householdEquivalent.note: People whose average daily household water use equals the site's daily water use.

generatorLocation.value: inside the building at the north-west outer wall: 14 on the 1st floor, 14 on the 2nd
generatorLocation.note: 'Die 28 dieselbetriebenen Notstrommotorenanlagen befinden sich an der nordwestlichen Außenwand im 1. und 2. Obergeschoss'.

stackCount.note: Exhaust of each group of 4 bundled into one stack.

stackHeight.note: Lower than the TA Luft nomogram would require; allowed because the generators run only a few hours a year, shown by dispersion modelling (TÜV Hessen T0003152).

testHoursPerGenerator.note: 3 h idle test, 4 h annual building-load test, 4 h load-bank test, 3 h emission measurement; one generator at a time. 392 h/yr across all 28.

plantShare.meaning: Share of the legal limit the 28 generators alone may add at each point.

totalCap.meaning: Maximum from ALL installations together, roof coolers included.

noiseReport.value: TÜV Hessen GmbH, schalltechnisches Gutachten Nr. T3509, 2021-03-25
noiseReport.howToGet: Part of the permit file at Regierungspräsidium Darmstadt; can be requested under HUIG.

generatorCount.note: 6 already approved under the 2022 building permit + 5 new.

generatorFuelInputEach.note: Feuerungswärmeleistung = heat in the fuel burned, not electrical output.

emergencyHoursMax.note: Cap for emergency operation (at least two generators running in parallel). Peak-shaving or grid-contract use is not allowed.

testHoursPerGenerator.note: Solo test runs incl. emission measurements; 231 h/yr across all 11. Running all at once for testing ('black building test') is not allowed.

dieselStorage.note: 3 underground tanks × 100 m³, plus 11 day tanks × 1.87 m³.

adblueStorage.note: 2 × 10 m³ urea solution for the SCR NOx catalysts fitted to every generator.

stackHeight.note: 5 shared stacks (2 flues each) + 1 single stack.

coolingWater.note: Authority's reply to a public objection: 'ausschließlich geschlossene Kühlkreiskreisläufe ohne Verdunstung und somit ohne Verbrauch von Wasser zu Kühlzwecken.' No industrial wastewater.

plantShare.meaning: Immissionsrichtwertanteile: the share of the legal noise limit that this generator plant alone may add at each point. Not a measurement.

points.note: Authority cut these by 6 dB(A) from the noise report's values because existing background noise was not assessed.

totalCap.meaning: Immissionsrichtwerte als Gesamtbelastung: the maximum from ALL installations together at each point. This covers roof coolers, transformers and the generators combined.

noiseLimits.peaks: Short noise peaks may not exceed the limit by more than 30 dB(A) by day or 20 dB(A) by night.
noiseLimits.tonality: Plant noise must not be impulsive, tonal or information-carrying, and must not cause harmful low-frequency noise.

noiseReport.value: TÜV Hessen GmbH, schalltechnisches Gutachten Nr. T3947, 2021-08-05; stated accuracy ±3 dB(A), treated by the authority as 0/−3 dB(A) (upper estimate)
noiseReport.howToGet: Part of the permit file at Regierungspräsidium Darmstadt; can be requested under the Hessian environmental-information law (HUIG).

cooling.caveats: Climate-dependent (hot, humid regions still need evaporation). Operators may not run at 45 °C in practice.

openItems.detail: In the noise reports TÜV Hessen T3947 (FRA22) and BEKON LA23-087 (FRA32). Not published; requestable from Regierungspräsidium Darmstadt under HUIG. The binding caps are already in this file.

siteData.note: Vantage has not published construction or staff numbers for FRA21. Its 2022 release mentions an office for up to 30 employees in Raunheim.

constructionPerMW.note: Ministry-commissioned study: 'Für größere Gebäude kann mit im Schnitt 16 Arbeitskräften pro MW gerechnet werden.' Employed 3 to 10 years depending on phasing.

operationPerMWLow.note: For buildings of 20 MW or more: 'maximal mit 0,3 bis 0,8 Arbeitsplätzen pro MW' (mainly security and maintenance).

itServicesPerMWLow.note: IT service companies using the capacity: 35 to 140 staff per MW of IT services. Not on site; anywhere in the world.

regionDirect.note: Frankfurt-Rhine-Main: 'Rund 2.900 Beschäftigte … gerade einmal 0,1 Prozent aller Arbeitsplätze'; about €1.3 bn a year of regional GDP and €405 m tax revenue.

itInfraPerMWLow.note: IT infrastructure operators who run the equipment inside datacenter buildings: 'mit 3 bis 25 Mitarbeitern pro Megawatt'. Not necessarily on site.

regionGDP.note: 'Die Rechenzentren tragen rund 1,3 Milliarden Euro jährlich zum BIP der Region Frankfurt-Rhein-Main bei.'

regionTax.note: 'Insgesamt gehen rund 405 Millionen Euro an Steuereinnahmen auf die Rechenzentrumsbranche zurück.'

claims.why: It depends on the cooling method: sealed-loop sites like FRA21 use almost no water, evaporative sites use a lot, and national figures are incomplete.

said.text: Federal Environment Minister Carsten Schneider: basic water needs 'dürfen nicht mit Großverbrauchern wie Rechenzentren konkurrieren'.

evidence.text: FRA21 reported a WUE of 0.01 L/kWh for 2025, about 3 m³ a day.
T-Systems Biere (evaporative) reported 1.03 L/kWh, about 145 m³ a day.
The federal Digital Ministry: 'Zum Wasserverbrauch durch Rechenzentren in Deutschland liegen nur begrenzt Zahlen vor.'

claims.claim: They create few, mostly temporary jobs.
claims.why: True for jobs on site: building needs hundreds of workers, running a large site needs a few dozen. Jobs at the companies using the computing are elsewhere.

evidence.text: Large sites (20 MW+) need at most 0.3–0.8 permanent jobs per MW; construction about 16 workers per MW.
About 2,900 people work in datacenters across Frankfurt-Rhine-Main: 0.1% of all jobs in the region.

claims.why: In Rhine-Main the local grid operator has no capacity left for new datacenters until the 2030s.

evidence.text: Grid operator Syna is booked out for datacenters; about 800 MW of new requests in one half-year, roughly Frankfurt's peak load; new applicants should plan for the early or mid-2030s.

claims.claim: They drive up household electricity prices.
claims.why: No German agency study on this was found. Most of this argument comes from the US debate.
True on paper, through yearly contracts and certificates. Nobody shows renewable power matched hour by hour.

evidence.text: FRA21 reports 100% renewable electricity on an annual balance.
The Öko-Institut recommends 'Deckung des Strombedarfs durch zeitgleich erzeugten Ökostrom' as a minimum standard.
A 2026 bill would move the legal 100% renewable deadline from 2027 to 2030.

claims.claim: Their waste heat could heat whole towns.
claims.why: The heat is lukewarm and needs heat pumps and heat networks. Today most of it is not used.

evidence.text: FRA21 released 118.7 GWh of heat at 27 °C in 2025 and reused none.
Industry body Bitkom: 'Viele Rechenzentren würden ihre Abwärme sogar kostenlos abgeben', but there are too few buyers.
New sites from July 2026 must reuse at least 10%.

claims.claim: AI will make datacenter energy use explode.
claims.why: Strong growth is well documented, but forecasts vary widely and datacenters stay a small share of total electricity.

evidence.text: Datacenters used around 1.5% of the world's electricity in 2024 (415 TWh), projected around 945 TWh by 2030, with large uncertainties.
German datacenters: about 21.3 TWh in 2025, against 526 TWh total German consumption.

claims.why: They are core infrastructure for the region, but their direct share of the economy is small.

evidence.text: Datacenters add about €1.3 bn a year to Frankfurt-Rhine-Main's GDP (about 0.5%) and about €405 m in taxes.
Frankfurt is home to DE-CIX, described by its operator as Europe's largest data hub.

claims.claim: Their diesel generators pollute the air.
claims.why: No measured air-quality impact is published. Running hours are capped by law and grid outages are rare.

evidence.text: FRA21's 28 generators may run at most 2,502 generator-hours a year in emergencies, plus 14 test hours each.
The average German electricity customer had 11.7 minutes of outage in 2024.

claims.why: Limits are set by permit, but no noise measurements or complaint records for Raunheim are public.

evidence.text: At the nearest homes, all equipment together may not exceed 40 dB(A) at night.
The noise report behind the permit (TÜV Hessen T3509) is not public.

noxFra22.note: 'durch den Einsatz von SCR-Katalysatoren auf 650 mg/m³ senken'.

irrelevance.unit: µg/m³ irrelevance threshold not exceeded (PM10, NO2)
irrelevance.note: TÜV Hessen air-pollution forecast: with running hours capped at 2,502 h/yr, the added fine dust and NO2 stays below the irrelevance threshold.

ffh.value: next to the EU nature reserve 'Wald bei Groß-Gerau' (FFH 6016-304); nitrogen and acid deposition assessed as not relevant

fra32Measures.value: insect-friendly lighting (max 3,000 K, no light above 85°), bird-safe glass, 10 cm gaps under fences for small animals, green berm

fra32Sealing.unit: share of plot that may be built over (GRZ)

groundwaterGoal.value: the local plan names reducing the effect of sealed ground on groundwater recharge as a goal

gridFactor2025.unit: g CO₂ per kWh, German electricity mix 2025 (estimate)

co2LocationBased.unit: t CO₂ in 2025 on the grid mix

co2MarketBased.value: about 0, because 100% is covered by renewable contracts or certificates
co2MarketBased.note: Market-based accounting counts contracts and certificates; location-based counts the actual grid. Both are defined by the GHG Protocol.

accounting.value: location-based = average grid; market-based = contracts and certificates

freeCooling.value: outside air cools most of the year; chillers needed above about 22 °C outside, for relatively few hours a year
freeCooling.note: 'über die meiste Zeit des Jahres mittels Außenluft frei gekühlt werden'; 'Steigt die Außenlufttemperatur auf Werte über ca. 22 °C, müssen weitere Maßnahmen ergriffen werden'.

freeCoolingHours.note: No published figure for how many hours a year a Frankfurt site like FRA21 can cool with outside air alone.

summerDays.unit: days a year at 25 °C or more

hotDays.unit: days a year at 30 °C or more

record.note: From recent daily data not yet fully quality-checked. Previous record 40.1 °C on 25 July 2019.

flatLoad.unit: % of its own peak: average load of a large hyperscale site
flatLoad.note: 'high, relatively flat utilization'; utility-funded research institute.

evapHotDays.value: outside air alone below 29 °C; evaporative cooling only on the hottest days (about 55 a year in Georgia, USA)

distanceRule.unit: dB quieter per doubling of distance (point source, open air)
distanceRule.note: Real sites also lose sound to buildings, walls, ground and air; this rule alone ignores that.

homesNear.unit: m, nearest permit address to FRA21 (Uhlandstraße 42a)
homesNear.formula: distance between OSM coordinates of the permit address and FRA21

homesFar.formula: distance between OSM coordinates of the permit address and FRA21

sourceLevel.note: How loud the roof coolers and generators are at the source is in the unpublished noise reports.
